title: Dividing by 2-Digit Divisors
seo_title: Grade 5 Dividing by 2-Digit Divisors Worksheets: Long Division (TEKS 5.3C, STAAR)
standard_text: 5.3C solve with proficiency for quotients of up to a four-digit dividend by a two-digit divisor using strategies and the standard algorithm
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 division worksheets for Texas TEKS 5.3C: divide up to 4-digit numbers by 2-digit divisors with estimates, long division, area models, zeros in the quotient, remainders and word problems. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Estimate with a rounded divisor, then divide, multiply, subtract, bring down.
key_sub: Write 0 when a place cannot be divided. Check: quotient × divisor + remainder = dividend.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • Round the divisor to estimate each digit of the quotient: 3,682 ÷ 25 is about 3,600 ÷ 25.
  • Divide, multiply, subtract, compare, bring down. If the difference is as big as the divisor, the estimate was too small.
  • Write 0 in the quotient when a place cannot be divided.
  • Check: quotient × divisor + remainder = dividend.

Examples

Example

2,436 ÷ 12

24 hundreds ÷ 12 = 2 hundreds

3 tens ÷ 12 = 0 tens

36 ÷ 12 = 3

Answer: 203

Example

Check 4,565 ÷ 87 = 52 R41

52 × 87 = 4,524

4,524 + 41 = 4,565

Answer: correct

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
An estimate that is too bigIf the product is larger than what you have, try a smaller digit.
Leaving out a 0 in the quotientEvery place after the first digit needs a digit.
A remainder as big as the divisorThen the quotient digit is too small.

faq.a: Solve with proficiency for quotients of up to a four-digit dividend by a two-digit divisor using strategies and the standard algorithm.

faq.q: How do you estimate with a 2-digit divisor?
faq.a: Round the divisor to the nearest ten and use a basic fact: 368 ÷ 42 is about 360 ÷ 40 = 9.

faq.q: What if my estimate is wrong?
faq.a: Adjust it: if the product is too big, try one less; if the difference is too big, try one more.

faq.q: How do you check a division answer?
faq.a: Multiply the quotient by the divisor and add the remainder.

sets.title: Divide with multiples of 10 and estimate

items.q: What is 120 ÷ 20?
items.e: Cross out one zero in each number: 120 ÷ 20 = 12 ÷ 2. 12 ÷ 2 = 6. Check: 6 × 20 = 120.

items.q: What is 490 ÷ 70?
items.e: Cross out one zero in each number: 490 ÷ 70 = 49 ÷ 7. 49 ÷ 7 = 7. Check: 7 × 70 = 490.

items.q: What is 540 ÷ 60?
items.e: Cross out one zero in each number: 540 ÷ 60 = 54 ÷ 6. 54 ÷ 6 = 9. Check: 9 × 60 = 540.

items.q: What is 240 ÷ 40?
items.e: Cross out one zero in each number: 240 ÷ 40 = 24 ÷ 4. 24 ÷ 4 = 6. Check: 6 × 40 = 240.

items.q: What is 3,500 ÷ 70?
items.e: Cross out one zero in each number: 3,500 ÷ 70 = 350 ÷ 7. 35 ÷ 7 = 5, so 350 ÷ 7 = 50. Be careful: cross out the same number of zeros in both numbers. Check: 50 × 70 = 3,500.

items.q: What is 8,100 ÷ 90?
items.e: Cross out one zero in each number: 8,100 ÷ 90 = 810 ÷ 9. 81 ÷ 9 = 9, so 810 ÷ 9 = 90. Be careful: cross out the same number of zeros in both numbers. Check: 90 × 90 = 8,100.

items.q: What is 2,000 ÷ 40?
items.e: Cross out one zero in each number: 2,000 ÷ 40 = 200 ÷ 4. 20 ÷ 4 = 5, so 200 ÷ 4 = 50. Be careful: 2,000 has 3 zeros, but one of them belongs to the fact 20 ÷ 4. Check: 50 × 40 = 2,000.

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ × 20 = 400
items.e: Think: what number times 20 is 400? That is 400 ÷ 20 = 40 ÷ 2 = 20. Check: 20 × 20 = 400.

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ × 70 = 420
items.e: Think: what number times 70 is 420? That is 420 ÷ 70 = 42 ÷ 7 = 6. Check: 6 × 70 = 420.

items.q: What number goes in the box? ☐ × 90 = 4,500
items.e: Think: what number times 90 is 4,500? That is 4,500 ÷ 90 = 450 ÷ 9 = 50. Check: 50 × 90 = 4,500.

items.q: Use compatible numbers to estimate 203 ÷ 68.
items.e: Round 68 to 70. A number close to 203 that 70 divides easily is 210, because 21 ÷ 7 = 3. 210 ÷ 70 = 3, so 203 ÷ 68 is about 3. (The exact answer is 2 R 67, which is close.)

items.q: Use compatible numbers to estimate 127 ÷ 42.
items.e: Round 42 to 40. A number close to 127 that 40 divides easily is 120, because 12 ÷ 4 = 3. 120 ÷ 40 = 3, so 127 ÷ 42 is about 3. (The exact answer is 3 R 1, which is close.)

items.q: Use compatible numbers to estimate 218 ÷ 67.
items.e: Round 67 to 70. A number close to 218 that 70 divides easily is 210, because 21 ÷ 7 = 3. 210 ÷ 70 = 3, so 218 ÷ 67 is about 3. (The exact answer is 3 R 17, which is close.)

items.q: Use compatible numbers to estimate 3,959 ÷ 76.
items.e: Round 76 to 80. A number close to 3,959 that 80 divides easily is 4,000, because 40 ÷ 8 = 5. 4,000 ÷ 80 = 50, so 3,959 ÷ 76 is about 50. (The exact answer is 52 R 7, which is close.)

items.q: Use compatible numbers to estimate 1,975 ÷ 39.
items.e: Round 39 to 40. A number close to 1,975 that 40 divides easily is 2,000, because 20 ÷ 4 = 5. 2,000 ÷ 40 = 50, so 1,975 ÷ 39 is about 50. (The exact answer is 50 R 25, which is close.)

items.q: Use compatible numbers to estimate 1,523 ÷ 31.
items.e: Round 31 to 30. A number close to 1,523 that 30 divides easily is 1,500, because 15 ÷ 3 = 5. 1,500 ÷ 30 = 50, so 1,523 ÷ 31 is about 50. (The exact answer is 49 R 4, which is close.)

items.q: Which numbers are best for estimating 234 ÷ 29?
items.e: Round 29 to 30. Then find a number near 234 that 30 divides easily: 24 ÷ 3 = 8, so use 240 ÷ 30 = 8. 200 ÷ 30 and 230 ÷ 30 do not come out evenly.

items.q: Which numbers are best for estimating 311 ÷ 78?
items.e: Round 78 to 80. Then find a number near 311 that 80 divides easily: 32 ÷ 8 = 4, so use 320 ÷ 80 = 4. 300 ÷ 80 and 310 ÷ 80 do not come out evenly.

items.q: Which numbers are best for estimating 712 ÷ 89?
items.e: Round 89 to 90. Then find a number near 712 that 90 divides easily: 72 ÷ 9 = 8, so use 720 ÷ 90 = 8. 700 ÷ 90 and 710 ÷ 90 do not come out evenly.

items.q: Which numbers are best for estimating 818 ÷ 88?
items.e: Round 88 to 90. Then find a number near 818 that 90 divides easily: 81 ÷ 9 = 9, so use 810 ÷ 90 = 9. 800 ÷ 90 and 820 ÷ 90 do not come out evenly.

items.q: Diego divides 184 ÷ 23. He rounds 23 to 20 and tries 9. 9 × 23 = 207, which is more than 184. What should he do next?
items.e: 207 is more than 184, so 9 is too big. Try 8: 8 × 23 = 184 and 184 − 184 = 0, which is less than 23. So 184 ÷ 23 = 8. Check: 8 × 23 = 184.

items.q: What is 224 ÷ 28?
items.e: Round 28 to 30. 224 ÷ 30 is about 7, so try 7. 7 × 28 = 196 and 224 − 196 = 28, which is not less than 28, so 7 is too small. Try 8. 8 × 28 = 224 and 224 − 224 = 0. Answer: 8. Check: 8 × 28 = 224.

items.q: What is the remainder when 301 is divided by 97?
items.e: The question asks for the remainder, not the quotient. Round 97 to 100. 301 ÷ 100 is about 3, so try 3. 3 × 97 = 291 and 301 − 291 = 10. Answer: 3 R 10. Check: 3 × 97 + 10 = 301.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: Round 31 to 30. 100 ÷ 30 is about 3, so try 3. 3 × 31 = 93 and 100 − 93 = 7. Answer: 3 R 7. Check: 3 × 31 + 7 = 100.

items.q: To divide 312 ÷ 46, which product should you use?
items.e: You need the greatest product that is not more than 312. 7 × 46 = 322 is too big, and 6 × 46 = 276 leaves 36, which is less than 46. So 312 ÷ 46 = 6 R 36.

items.q: What is the remainder when 292 is divided by 35?
items.e: The question asks for the remainder, not the quotient. Round 35 to 40. 292 ÷ 40 is about 7, so try 7. 7 × 35 = 245 and 292 − 245 = 47, which is not less than 35, so 7 is too small. Try 8. 8 × 35 = 280 and 292 − 280 = 12. Answer: 8 R 12. Check: 8 × 35 + 12 = 292.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: Round 74 to 70. 222 ÷ 70 is about 3, so try 3. 3 × 74 = 222 and 222 − 222 = 0. Answer: 3. Check: 3 × 74 = 222.

items.q: What is 619 ÷ 76?
items.e: Round 76 to 80. 619 ÷ 80 is about 7, so try 7. 7 × 76 = 532 and 619 − 532 = 87, which is not less than 76, so 7 is too small. Try 8. 8 × 76 = 608 and 619 − 608 = 11. Answer: 8 R 11. Check: 8 × 76 + 11 = 619.

items.q: Ethan divides 258 ÷ 86. He rounds 86 to 90 and tries 2. 2 × 86 = 172 and 258 − 172 = 86. What should he do next?
items.e: The difference 86 is not less than the divisor 86, so 86 fits one more time. Try 3: 3 × 86 = 258 and 258 − 258 = 0. So 258 ÷ 86 = 3. Check: 3 × 86 = 258.

items.q: Emma divides 112 ÷ 14. She rounds 14 to 10 and tries 9. 9 × 14 = 126, which is more than 112. What should she do next?
items.e: 126 is more than 112, so 9 is too big. Try 8: 8 × 14 = 112 and 112 − 112 = 0, which is less than 14. So 112 ÷ 14 = 8. Check: 8 × 14 = 112.

items.q: What is 144 ÷ 24?
items.e: Round 24 to 20. 144 ÷ 20 is about 7, so try 7. 7 × 24 = 168, which is more than 144, so 7 is too big. Try 6. 6 × 24 = 144 and 144 − 144 = 0. Answer: 6. Check: 6 × 24 = 144.

items.q: Ximena divides 267 ÷ 89. She rounds 89 to 90 and tries 2. 2 × 89 = 178 and 267 − 178 = 89. What should she do next?
items.e: The difference 89 is not less than the divisor 89, so 89 fits one more time. Try 3: 3 × 89 = 267 and 267 − 267 = 0. So 267 ÷ 89 = 3. Check: 3 × 89 = 267.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: Round 18 to 20. 126 ÷ 20 is about 6, so try 6. 6 × 18 = 108 and 126 − 108 = 18, which is not less than 18, so 6 is too small. Try 7. 7 × 18 = 126 and 126 − 126 = 0. Answer: 7. Check: 7 × 18 = 126.

items.q: What is 813 ÷ 93?
items.e: Round 93 to 90. 813 ÷ 90 is about 9, so try 9. 9 × 93 = 837, which is more than 813, so 9 is too big. Try 8. 8 × 93 = 744 and 813 − 744 = 69. Answer: 8 R 69. Check: 8 × 93 + 69 = 813.

items.q: To divide 496 ÷ 67, which product should you use?
items.e: You need the greatest product that is not more than 496. 8 × 67 = 536 is too big, and 7 × 67 = 469 leaves 27, which is less than 67. So 496 ÷ 67 = 7 R 27.

items.q: Jayden divides 390 ÷ 65. He rounds 65 to 70 and tries 5. 5 × 65 = 325 and 390 − 325 = 65. What should he do next?
items.e: The difference 65 is not less than the divisor 65, so 65 fits one more time. Try 6: 6 × 65 = 390 and 390 − 390 = 0. So 390 ÷ 65 = 6. Check: 6 × 65 = 390.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: Round 84 to 80. 578 ÷ 80 is about 7, so try 7. 7 × 84 = 588, which is more than 578, so 7 is too big. Try 6. 6 × 84 = 504 and 578 − 504 = 74. Answer: 6 R 74. Check: 6 × 84 + 74 = 578.

items.q: Josiah divides 104 ÷ 13. He rounds 13 to 10 and tries 9. 9 × 13 = 117, which is more than 104. What should he do next?
items.e: 117 is more than 104, so 9 is too big. Try 8: 8 × 13 = 104 and 104 − 104 = 0, which is less than 13. So 104 ÷ 13 = 8. Check: 8 × 13 = 104.

items.q: What is the remainder when 149 is divided by 46?
items.e: The question asks for the remainder, not the quotient. Round 46 to 50. 149 ÷ 50 is about 2, so try 2. 2 × 46 = 92 and 149 − 92 = 57, which is not less than 46, so 2 is too small. Try 3. 3 × 46 = 138 and 149 − 138 = 11. Answer: 3 R 11. Check: 3 × 46 + 11 = 149.

items.q: To divide 263 ÷ 37, which product should you use?
items.e: You need the greatest product that is not more than 263. 8 × 37 = 296 is too big, and 7 × 37 = 259 leaves 4, which is less than 37. So 263 ÷ 37 = 7 R 4.

sets.title: Two-digit quotients: long division and area models

items.q: What is 5,755 ÷ 67?
items.e: 57 is less than 67, so start with 575. 575 ÷ 67 = 8: 8 × 67 = 536, 575 − 536 = 39. Bring down 5: 395 ÷ 67 = 5: 5 × 67 = 335, 395 − 335 = 60. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 60. Answer: 85 R 60. Check: 85 × 67 + 60 = 5,755.

items.q: Divide.
What is 656 ÷ 16?
Divide.
items.e: 62 is less than 75, so start with 624. 624 ÷ 75 = 8: 8 × 75 = 600, 624 − 600 = 24. Bring down 9: 249 ÷ 75 = 3: 3 × 75 = 225, 249 − 225 = 24. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 24. Answer: 83 R 24. Check: 83 × 75 + 24 = 6,249.

items.q: Divide.
You divide 5,374 ÷ 21 with long division. Above which place do you write the first digit of the quotient?
items.e: 53 is at least 21, so start with 53 hundreds: 53 ÷ 21 = 2. The quotient is 255 R 19.

items.q: Use the area model to find 1,702 ÷ 37.
items.e: The model splits 1,702 into 1,110 + 370 + 222. Divide each part by 37: 1,110 ÷ 37 = 30, 370 ÷ 37 = 10, 222 ÷ 37 = 6. Add the partial quotients: 30 + 10 + 6 = 46. Check: 46 × 37 = 1,702.

items.q: You divide 3,390 ÷ 83 with long division. Above which place do you write the first digit of the quotient?
items.e: 33 is less than 83, so there are no hundreds in the quotient. Start with 339 tens: 339 ÷ 83 = 4. The quotient is 40 R 70.

items.q: What is 741 ÷ 57?
How many digits does the quotient of 1,595 ÷ 82 have?
items.e: 15 is less than 82, so the quotient has no hundreds. Start with 159 tens. 1,595 ÷ 82 = 19 R 37, which has 2 digits.

items.q: What is 2,074 ÷ 71?
items.e: 20 is less than 71, so start with 207. 207 ÷ 71 = 2: 2 × 71 = 142, 207 − 142 = 65. Bring down 4: 654 ÷ 71 = 9: 9 × 71 = 639, 654 − 639 = 15. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 15. Answer: 29 R 15. Check: 29 × 71 + 15 = 2,074.

items.q: What is 2,470 ÷ 38?
Use the area model to find 1,584 ÷ 48.
items.e: The model splits 1,584 into 1,440 + 144. Divide each part by 48: 1,440 ÷ 48 = 30, 144 ÷ 48 = 3. Add the partial quotients: 30 + 3 = 33. Check: 33 × 48 = 1,584.

items.q: Ms. Rivera uses partial quotients to find 1,419 ÷ 33: 33 × 30 = 990, and 1,419 − 990 = 429. 33 × 10 = 330, and 429 − 330 = 99. 33 × 3 = 99, and 99 − 99 = 0. What is the quotient?
items.e: Add the partial quotients: 30 + 10 + 3 = 43. Check: 43 × 33 = 1,419.

items.q: Divide.
Mr. Chen uses partial quotients to find 1,445 ÷ 17: 17 × 70 = 1,190, and 1,445 − 1,190 = 255. 17 × 10 = 170, and 255 − 170 = 85. 17 × 5 = 85, and 85 − 85 = 0. What is the quotient?
items.e: Add the partial quotients: 70 + 10 + 5 = 85. Check: 85 × 17 = 1,445.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: 12 is less than 55, so start with 124. 124 ÷ 55 = 2: 2 × 55 = 110, 124 − 110 = 14. Bring down 5: 145 ÷ 55 = 2: 2 × 55 = 110, 145 − 110 = 35. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 35. Answer: 22 R 35. Check: 22 × 55 + 35 = 1,245.

items.q: What is 1,080 ÷ 45?
Divide.
Use the area model to find 1,474 ÷ 22.
items.e: The model splits 1,474 into 1,320 + 154. Divide each part by 22: 1,320 ÷ 22 = 60, 154 ÷ 22 = 7. Add the partial quotients: 60 + 7 = 67. Check: 67 × 22 = 1,474.

sets.title: Zeros in the quotient, remainders and checking

items.q: Divide.
items.e: 8 is less than 19, so start with 81. 81 ÷ 19 = 4: 4 × 19 = 76, 81 − 76 = 5. Bring down 7: 57 ÷ 19 = 3: 3 × 19 = 57, 57 − 57 = 0. Bring down 0: 19 does not fit into 0, so write 0 in the quotient. Answer: 430. Check: 430 × 19 = 8,170.

items.q: 2,387 ÷ 72 = 33 R 11. Which expression checks this answer? It should equal 2,387.
items.e: Multiply the quotient by the divisor, then add the remainder: 72 × 33 = 2,376, 2,376 + 11 = 2,387. It matches the dividend, so the answer is right.

items.q: 6,338 ÷ 96 = 66 R 2. Which expression checks this answer? It should equal 6,338.
items.e: Multiply the quotient by the divisor, then add the remainder: 96 × 66 = 6,336, 6,336 + 2 = 6,338. It matches the dividend, so the answer is right.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: 46 is less than 57, so start with 466. 466 ÷ 57 = 8: 8 × 57 = 456, 466 − 456 = 10. Bring down 2: 102 ÷ 57 = 1: 1 × 57 = 57, 102 − 57 = 45. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 45. Answer: 81 R 45. Check: 81 × 57 + 45 = 4,662.

items.q: Gabriel says 2,906 ÷ 49 = 58 R 64. What mistake did he make?
items.e: The remainder must be less than the divisor. 64 is more than 49, so 49 fits one more time: 64 − 49 = 15. The answer is 59 R 15. Check: 59 × 49 + 15 = 2,906.

items.q: What is 4,209 ÷ 42?
items.e: 4 is less than 42, so start with 42. 42 ÷ 42 = 1: 1 × 42 = 42, 42 − 42 = 0. Bring down 0: 42 does not fit into 0, so write 0 in the quotient. Bring down 9: 42 does not fit into 9, so write 0 in the quotient. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 9. Answer: 100 R 9. Check: 100 × 42 + 9 = 4,209.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: 2 is less than 19, so start with 20. 20 ÷ 19 = 1: 1 × 19 = 19, 20 − 19 = 1. Bring down 5: 19 does not fit into 15, so write 0 in the quotient. Bring down 2: 152 ÷ 19 = 8: 8 × 19 = 152, 152 − 152 = 0. Answer: 108. Check: 108 × 19 = 2,052.

items.q: Josiah says 1,533 ÷ 28 = 53 R 49. What mistake did he make?
items.e: The remainder must be less than the divisor. 49 is more than 28, so 28 fits one more time: 49 − 28 = 21. The answer is 54 R 21. Check: 54 × 28 + 21 = 1,533.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: 54 is less than 61, so start with 542. 542 ÷ 61 = 8: 8 × 61 = 488, 542 − 488 = 54. Bring down 7: 547 ÷ 61 = 8: 8 × 61 = 488, 547 − 488 = 59. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 59. Answer: 88 R 59. Check: 88 × 61 + 59 = 5,427.

items.q: In a division problem, the divisor is 34, the quotient is 56 and the remainder is 12. What is the dividend?
items.e: Dividend = quotient × divisor + remainder: 56 × 34 = 1,904, 1,904 + 12 = 1,916. Check: 1,916 ÷ 34 = 56 R 12.

items.q: What is 2,787 ÷ 78?
items.e: 27 is less than 78, so start with 278. 278 ÷ 78 = 3: 3 × 78 = 234, 278 − 234 = 44. Bring down 7: 447 ÷ 78 = 5: 5 × 78 = 390, 447 − 390 = 57. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 57. Answer: 35 R 57. Check: 35 × 78 + 57 = 2,787.

items.q: What is 7,730 ÷ 79?
items.e: 77 is less than 79, so start with 773. 773 ÷ 79 = 9: 9 × 79 = 711, 773 − 711 = 62. Bring down 0: 620 ÷ 79 = 7: 7 × 79 = 553, 620 − 553 = 67. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 67. Answer: 97 R 67. Check: 97 × 79 + 67 = 7,730.

items.q: What is 2,187 ÷ 31?
items.e: 21 is less than 31, so start with 218. 218 ÷ 31 = 7: 7 × 31 = 217, 218 − 217 = 1. Bring down 7: 31 does not fit into 17, so write 0 in the quotient. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 17. Answer: 70 R 17. Check: 70 × 31 + 17 = 2,187.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: 24 is less than 71, so start with 241. 241 ÷ 71 = 3: 3 × 71 = 213, 241 − 213 = 28. Bring down 9: 289 ÷ 71 = 4: 4 × 71 = 284, 289 − 284 = 5. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 5. Answer: 34 R 5. Check: 34 × 71 + 5 = 2,419.

items.q: Divide.
items.e: 8 is less than 21, so start with 84. 84 ÷ 21 = 4: 4 × 21 = 84, 84 − 84 = 0. Bring down 8: 21 does not fit into 8, so write 0 in the quotient. Bring down 4: 84 ÷ 21 = 4: 4 × 21 = 84, 84 − 84 = 0. Answer: 404. Check: 404 × 21 = 8,484.

items.q: Luis says 1,304 ÷ 13 = 1 R 4. What mistake did he make?
items.e: Check his answer: 1 × 13 + 4 = 17, not 1,304. When 13 does not fit, write 0 in the quotient. 1 is less than 13, so start with 13. 13 ÷ 13 = 1: 1 × 13 = 13, 13 − 13 = 0. Bring down 0: 13 does not fit into 0, so write 0 in the quotient. Bring down 4: 13 does not fit into 4, so write 0 in the quotient. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 4. Answer: 100 R 4. Check: 100 × 13 + 4 = 1,304.

items.q: Isabella says 4,436 ÷ 22 = 21 R 14. What mistake did she make?
items.e: Check her answer: 21 × 22 + 14 = 476, not 4,436. When 22 does not fit, write 0 in the quotient. 4 is less than 22, so start with 44. 44 ÷ 22 = 2: 2 × 22 = 44, 44 − 44 = 0. Bring down 3: 22 does not fit into 3, so write 0 in the quotient. Bring down 6: 36 ÷ 22 = 1: 1 × 22 = 22, 36 − 22 = 14. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 14. Answer: 201 R 14. Check: 201 × 22 + 14 = 4,436.

items.q: 1,369 ÷ 49 = 27 R 46. Which expression checks this answer? It should equal 1,369.
items.e: Multiply the quotient by the divisor, then add the remainder: 49 × 27 = 1,323, 1,323 + 46 = 1,369. It matches the dividend, so the answer is right.

items.q: What is 4,994 ÷ 47?
items.e: 4 is less than 47, so start with 49. 49 ÷ 47 = 1: 1 × 47 = 47, 49 − 47 = 2. Bring down 9: 47 does not fit into 29, so write 0 in the quotient. Bring down 4: 294 ÷ 47 = 6: 6 × 47 = 282, 294 − 282 = 12. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 12. Answer: 106 R 12. Check: 106 × 47 + 12 = 4,994.

items.q: What is 6,847 ÷ 93?
items.e: 68 is less than 93, so start with 684. 684 ÷ 93 = 7: 7 × 93 = 651, 684 − 651 = 33. Bring down 7: 337 ÷ 93 = 3: 3 × 93 = 279, 337 − 279 = 58. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 58. Answer: 73 R 58. Check: 73 × 93 + 58 = 6,847.

sets.title: Word problems: what to do with the remainder

items.q: A factory has 3,473 crayons. It puts 24 crayons in each box. How many boxes can it fill completely?
items.e: Divide: 3 is less than 24, so start with 34. 34 ÷ 24 = 1: 1 × 24 = 24, 34 − 24 = 10. Bring down 7: 107 ÷ 24 = 4: 4 × 24 = 96, 107 − 96 = 11. Bring down 3: 113 ÷ 24 = 4: 4 × 24 = 96, 113 − 96 = 17. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 17. So 3,473 ÷ 24 = 144 R 17. Check: 144 × 24 + 17 = 3,473. The 17 crayons left over are not enough to fill another box, so leave the remainder out. The answer is 144 boxes.

items.q: Ava has 366 beads. She makes necklaces with 24 beads each and says she can make 15 necklaces with 6 beads left over. Which expression checks her answer? It should equal 366.
items.e: Multiply the number of necklaces by the beads on each one, then add the beads left over: 15 × 24 = 360, 360 + 6 = 366. That is all 366 beads, so her answer is right.

items.q: A school is taking 334 students on a field trip. Each bus holds 52 students. How many buses are needed to take everyone?
items.e: Divide: 33 is less than 52, so start with 334. 334 ÷ 52 = 6: 6 × 52 = 312, 334 − 312 = 22. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 22. So 334 ÷ 52 = 6 R 22. Check: 6 × 52 + 22 = 334. 6 buses are not enough: 22 students still need a bus. Add 1 more, so the answer is 7 buses.

items.q: Ms. Rivera has 635 sheets of paper. She gives the same number of sheets to each of her 27 students, as many as she can. How many sheets are left over?
items.e: Divide: 6 is less than 27, so start with 63. 63 ÷ 27 = 2: 2 × 27 = 54, 63 − 54 = 9. Bring down 5: 95 ÷ 27 = 3: 3 × 27 = 81, 95 − 81 = 14. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 14. So 635 ÷ 27 = 23 R 14. Check: 23 × 27 + 14 = 635. The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder: 14 sheets.

items.q: Zoe has a roll of ribbon that is 381 inches long. She cuts it into pieces that are each 18 inches long. How many pieces can she cut?
items.e: Divide: 3 is less than 18, so start with 38. 38 ÷ 18 = 2: 2 × 18 = 36, 38 − 36 = 2. Bring down 1: 21 ÷ 18 = 1: 1 × 18 = 18, 21 − 18 = 3. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 3. So 381 ÷ 18 = 21 R 3. Check: 21 × 18 + 3 = 381. The 3 inches left over are not enough to cut another piece, so leave the remainder out. The answer is 21 pieces.

items.q: Carlos shares 388 stickers equally among 24 classmates. Each classmate gets as many as possible. How many stickers are left over?
items.e: Divide: 3 is less than 24, so start with 38. 38 ÷ 24 = 1: 1 × 24 = 24, 38 − 24 = 14. Bring down 8: 148 ÷ 24 = 6: 6 × 24 = 144, 148 − 144 = 4. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 4. So 388 ÷ 24 = 16 R 4. Check: 16 × 24 + 4 = 388. The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder: 4 stickers.

items.q: A school has $596 to spend on calculators. Each calculator costs $14. How many calculators can the school buy?
items.e: Divide: 5 is less than 14, so start with 59. 59 ÷ 14 = 4: 4 × 14 = 56, 59 − 56 = 3. Bring down 6: 36 ÷ 14 = 2: 2 × 14 = 28, 36 − 28 = 8. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 8. So 596 ÷ 14 = 42 R 8. Check: 42 × 14 + 8 = 596. The 8 dollars left over are not enough to buy another calculator, so leave the remainder out. The answer is 42 calculators.

items.q: A concert hall needs seats for 641 people. Each row has 24 seats. How many rows are needed so everyone has a seat?
items.e: Divide: 6 is less than 24, so start with 64. 64 ÷ 24 = 2: 2 × 24 = 48, 64 − 48 = 16. Bring down 1: 161 ÷ 24 = 6: 6 × 24 = 144, 161 − 144 = 17. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 17. So 641 ÷ 24 = 26 R 17. Check: 26 × 24 + 17 = 641. 26 rows are not enough: 17 people still need a seat. Add 1 more, so the answer is 27 rows.

items.q: A bakery is delivering 746 muffins. Each tray holds 24 muffins. How many trays are needed for all the muffins?
items.e: Divide: 7 is less than 24, so start with 74. 74 ÷ 24 = 3: 3 × 24 = 72, 74 − 72 = 2. Bring down 6: 26 ÷ 24 = 1: 1 × 24 = 24, 26 − 24 = 2. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 2. So 746 ÷ 24 = 31 R 2. Check: 31 × 24 + 2 = 746. 31 trays are not enough: 2 muffins still need a tray. Add 1 more, so the answer is 32 trays.

items.q: A bakery made 1,659 cookies. It packs them in boxes of 36 and fills as many boxes as it can. How many cookies are not in a box?
items.e: Divide: 16 is less than 36, so start with 165. 165 ÷ 36 = 4: 4 × 36 = 144, 165 − 144 = 21. Bring down 9: 219 ÷ 36 = 6: 6 × 36 = 216, 219 − 216 = 3. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 3. So 1,659 ÷ 36 = 46 R 3. Check: 46 × 36 + 3 = 1,659. The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder: 3 cookies.

items.q: There are 195 cars waiting for a ferry. The ferry carries 22 cars on each trip. How many trips does the ferry need to make?
items.e: Divide: 19 is less than 22, so start with 195. 195 ÷ 22 = 8: 8 × 22 = 176, 195 − 176 = 19. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 19. So 195 ÷ 22 = 8 R 19. Check: 8 × 22 + 19 = 195. 8 trips are not enough: 19 cars still need a trip. Add 1 more, so the answer is 9 trips.

items.q: Aaliyah has $174 saved. Concert tickets cost $35 each. How many tickets can she buy?
items.e: Divide: 17 is less than 35, so start with 174. 174 ÷ 35 = 4: 4 × 35 = 140, 174 − 140 = 34. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 34. So 174 ÷ 35 = 4 R 34. Check: 4 × 35 + 34 = 174. The 34 dollars left over are not enough to buy another ticket, so leave the remainder out. The answer is 4 tickets.

items.q: A train travels 1,416 miles in 12 hours. It goes the same distance every hour. How many miles does it travel each hour?
items.e: Divide: 1 is less than 12, so start with 14. 14 ÷ 12 = 1: 1 × 12 = 12, 14 − 12 = 2. Bring down 1: 21 ÷ 12 = 1: 1 × 12 = 12, 21 − 12 = 9. Bring down 6: 96 ÷ 12 = 8: 8 × 12 = 96, 96 − 96 = 0. So 1,416 ÷ 12 = 118. Check: 118 × 12 = 1,416. There is no remainder, so the answer is 118 miles.

items.q: A farm collected 1,377 eggs. It packs them in cartons of 18. How many cartons can it fill completely?
items.e: Divide: 13 is less than 18, so start with 137. 137 ÷ 18 = 7: 7 × 18 = 126, 137 − 126 = 11. Bring down 7: 117 ÷ 18 = 6: 6 × 18 = 108, 117 − 108 = 9. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 9. So 1,377 ÷ 18 = 76 R 9. Check: 76 × 18 + 9 = 1,377. The 9 eggs left over are not enough to fill another carton, so leave the remainder out. The answer is 76 cartons.

items.q: An orchard picked 2,278 apples. The apples are packed in crates of 88, and every crate is filled. How many apples are left over?
items.e: Divide: 22 is less than 88, so start with 227. 227 ÷ 88 = 2: 2 × 88 = 176, 227 − 176 = 51. Bring down 8: 518 ÷ 88 = 5: 5 × 88 = 440, 518 − 440 = 78. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 78. So 2,278 ÷ 88 = 25 R 78. Check: 25 × 88 + 78 = 2,278. The question asks how many are left over. That is the remainder: 78 apples.

items.q: A theater sold tickets for $2,375 in all. Each ticket cost $25. How many tickets did the theater sell?
items.e: Divide: 23 is less than 25, so start with 237. 237 ÷ 25 = 9: 9 × 25 = 225, 237 − 225 = 12. Bring down 5: 125 ÷ 25 = 5: 5 × 25 = 125, 125 − 125 = 0. So 2,375 ÷ 25 = 95. Check: 95 × 25 = 2,375. There is no remainder, so the answer is 95 tickets.

items.q: A summer camp has 156 campers. Each cabin group needs exactly 14 campers. How many full groups can be made?
items.e: Divide: 1 is less than 14, so start with 15. 15 ÷ 14 = 1: 1 × 14 = 14, 15 − 14 = 1. Bring down 6: 16 ÷ 14 = 1: 1 × 14 = 14, 16 − 14 = 2. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 2. So 156 ÷ 14 = 11 R 2. Check: 11 × 14 + 2 = 156. The 2 campers left over are not enough to make another group, so leave the remainder out. The answer is 11 groups.

items.q: A school raised $1,335 at a fun fair. It shares the money equally among 15 classes. How much money does each class get?
items.e: Divide: 13 is less than 15, so start with 133. 133 ÷ 15 = 8: 8 × 15 = 120, 133 − 120 = 13. Bring down 5: 135 ÷ 15 = 9: 9 × 15 = 135, 135 − 135 = 0. So 1,335 ÷ 15 = 89. Check: 89 × 15 = 1,335. There is no remainder, so the answer is $89.

items.q: There are 375 guests at a banquet. Each table seats 14 guests. How many tables are needed so every guest has a seat?
items.e: Divide: 3 is less than 14, so start with 37. 37 ÷ 14 = 2: 2 × 14 = 28, 37 − 28 = 9. Bring down 5: 95 ÷ 14 = 6: 6 × 14 = 84, 95 − 84 = 11. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 11. So 375 ÷ 14 = 26 R 11. Check: 26 × 14 + 11 = 375. 26 tables are not enough: 11 guests still need a seat. Add 1 more, so the answer is 27 tables.

items.q: A school library is moving 1,555 books. Each box holds 36 books. How many boxes are needed to pack all the books?
items.e: Divide: 15 is less than 36, so start with 155. 155 ÷ 36 = 4: 4 × 36 = 144, 155 − 144 = 11. Bring down 5: 115 ÷ 36 = 3: 3 × 36 = 108, 115 − 108 = 7. Nothing is left to bring down, so the remainder is 7. So 1,555 ÷ 36 = 43 R 7. Check: 43 × 36 + 7 = 1,555. 43 boxes are not enough: 7 books still need a box. Add 1 more, so the answer is 44 boxes.
